category_summary: **Accessibility & community building (lead item):** The clear winner is the official **@NousResearch** [reply to **@AviSchiffmann**](/?date=2026-11-25&category=social#item-82b26b0e5e17) noting that 'scrappy users' are building wonderful things with **free and heavily discounted models** — the week's top post by far (294 likes, ~7.9k views) and an on-mission message that cheap, broad model access is fueling grassroots projects across the **Hermes** ecosystem; it doubles as a cultural statement that fits the newsletter's open-weights ethos. **Official account engagement (short replies):** Three low-content replies round out the section — a playful confirmation to **@kerwinv101** (['Yes it's his hair'](/?date=2026-11-25&category=social#item-ff4d65f2b62e)) in a thread tagging **@NVIDIAAI** (18 likes), an affirming ['Always'](/?date=2026-11-25&category=social#item-6152abf7d957) to **@bippolaroid** (8 likes, ~1.2k views), and a one-word ['Sick'](/?date=2026-11-25&category=social#item-33e6326f366f) reacting to a **@Teknium**-adjacent demo (**@__RobertG__** thread, 1 like, 427 views); these are tie-broken by residual engagement, with the Teknium nod flagged as a possible early signal of in-house work worth watching in future issues. **Sentiment:** Community tone is positive, and the official account reads as approachable, quick to reply, and community-first; engagement clusters around the substantive accessibility statement rather than the banter, so the three replies carry personality and brand-voice value more than standalone news value — worth including mainly to convey the team's responsive, scrappy culture.
